title: Texas hunting licenses and public-land permits
intro: A hunting license is required to hunt in Texas. Public hunting on Annual Public Hunting (APH) lands also needs the APH permit package or the applicable e-postcard / drawn permit. Corps lakes may require a separate Recreation.gov or lake permit. Confirm current fees before you buy.

whereToBuy.title: Online
whereToBuy.body: Buy resident and nonresident hunting licenses, stamps, and many tags at the TPWD license sales site. Print or carry the digital license.

whereToBuy.title: License retailer or TPWD office
whereToBuy.body: License agents and some TPWD offices sell hunting licenses and stamps in person.

whereToBuy.title: Annual Public Hunting permit
whereToBuy.body: Buy the APH package for walk-in public hunting lands listed in the Public Hunting Lands Map Booklet. Some units also use e-postcard drawings or regular daily permits.

whereToBuy.title: Corps of Engineers lakes
whereToBuy.body: Many Fort Worth District lakes require a hunting permit through Recreation.gov or the lake office in addition to a Texas hunting license.

deadlines.name: License year
deadlines.detail: Most Texas hunting licenses run September 1 through August 31. Buy before you hunt.

deadlines.name: E-postcard drawings
deadlines.detail: Application windows vary by unit. Check each unit’s TPWD details page and e-postcard listing.

residencyRules: Nonresidents may hunt the same legal birds and animals as residents with a Non-resident General Hunting License (including white-tailed and mule deer, pronghorn, and bighorn sheep), plus required endorsements/tags.
Senior resident and resident combination hunting/fishing licenses are residents only (shown as — for nonresidents in the fee table).

Annual Public Hunting (APH) permits are sold to residents and nonresidents at the same prices; drawn e-postcard and special hunts follow each unit’s TPWD listing rather than a statewide nonresident ban.
